title: Order count by status
statement_markdown: Return every order status and its number of orders. Sort by count descending, then status alphabetically to break ties.

examples.explanation: This output comes from the visible sample data.

hints: Group rows by status and count each group.
Add a second ORDER BY key so equal counts have deterministic order.
explanation: COUNT(*) measures rows in each status group. Sorting by count highlights the most common status and the status tie-breaker prevents unstable output. A common mistake is omitting status from GROUP BY. Conditional aggregation is useful when statuses should become separate columns.
reference_solution: SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS count FROM orders GROUP BY status ORDER BY count DESC, status
